props.gloss_en: the incident of David and Amnon is neither read nor translated (the lemma's reading; 25a.16 prints נקראין ולא מתרגמין -- header)
the Tosefta: the incident of Amnon and Tamar is read and translated
this [the mishnah's 'not read'] is where it is written 'Amnon son of David'
that [the Tosefta's 'read and translated'] is where it is written plain 'Amnon'
all verses written in the Torah coarsely are read refinedly: yishgalena as yishkavena, bafolim as batechorim, chiryonim as divyonim, choreihem / meimei shineihem as tzo'atam / meimei ragleihem
the baraita: lemacharaot ('latrines', 2 Kgs 10:27) is read lemotza'ot
R' Yehoshua ben Korcha: lemacharaot is read as written
R' Yehoshua ben Korcha's reason: because it is a disgrace to idolatry
Rav Nachman: all mockery is forbidden
...except mockery of idolatry, which is permitted
Rav Nachman's source: 'Bel bows down, Nevo stoops' (Isa 46:1), and 'they stoop, they bow down together, they could not deliver the burden' (Isa 46:2)
R' Yannai: [it is learned] from here: 'the inhabitants of Samaria dread for the calves of Beit Aven ... for its glory (kevodo), because it has departed from it' (Hos 10:5)
R' Yannai: do not read kevodo ('its glory') but keveido ('its heaviness')
a Jew is permitted to say to a gentile: take the idol and put it in its shin-tav
Rav Ashi: one of ill repute -- it is permitted to disgrace him with gimel-shin
one of good repute -- it is permitted to praise him
and whoever praises him -- blessings will rest on his head
